title: Descent of compatible functors from an object-and-arrow filtered colimit
statement: Let J be a small filtered category, F : J → Cat of small categories, and L a cocone such that Cat.objects.mapCocone L and Cat.arrows.mapCocone L are colimits of sets. For any category D (with arbitrary object and hom universes), a strictly compatible family v_j : F.obj j → D descends to a functor V : L.pt → D with (L.ι.app j).toFunctor ⋙ V = v_j for every j. Arrows are as in def-weil-pbc-arrows-functor.

source.place: Tag 09YL, first paragraph of proof; universal-property verification written by R2

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Types.isColimit_iff_coconeTypesIsColimit and Functor.CoconeTypes.IsColimit.exists_desc to the compatible object maps and arrow maps. This gives maps O to D and A to Arrow D with the required representative formulas, without any universe bound on D. Arrow joint surjectivity identifies the endpoints of A with O; conjugating A.hom by these endpoint equalities gives the morphism map M.

Object joint surjectivity and the representative formula prove that M preserves identities. For composition, jointly_surjective_of_isColimit₂ lifts both arrows to one stage. The middle endpoints have equal images in the object colimit; isColimit_eq_iff' moves them to a later stage where they are equal. Insert eqToHom for that equality to form a composable pair. The cocone equation and equality of arrows under endpoint transport identify its images with the original arrows. Functoriality of the stage functor v proves preservation of composition. Assemble O and M into V and use Functor.hext and the representative formulas to prove the strict restriction equalities.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_filteredColimit_functor_descent
    (J : Type u) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J]
    (F : J ⥤ Cat.{u, u}) (L : Cocone F)
    (hobjects : Nonempty (IsColimit (Cat.objects.mapCocone L)))
    (harrows : Nonempty (IsColimit (Cat.arrows.mapCocone L)))
    (D : Type v) [Category.{w} D] (v : ∀ j : J, F.obj j ⥤ D)
    (hcompat : ∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k), (F.map a).toFunctor ⋙ v k = v j) :
    ∃ V : L.pt ⥤ D, ∀ j : J, (L.ι.app j).toFunctor ⋙ V = v j
